review_comments: Look at the other tests that use getters (grep for `TGetter`), and add values to those. The second parameter for that can be the value. For example: `TGetter("foo", TString("value"))`

I created a new refactoring [issue](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/63667) about this case and a similar one we discussed on structure properties separation PR, to remove some dedicated test classes.

About just putting a value there. I'm pretty sure it works only for simple getters (autoexpandable), without a custom return. In case I'm wrong then I will exchange the mechanism with your suggestion while refactoring.
Having the value there also will check the value returned by the getter, which can be affected by fields/properties getting overriden, or shadowed.
